evals.prompt: This is the Larder repo. I'm onboarding two new developers next week. Can you make an interactive diagram, one HTML file I can send them, of what happens when a customer places an order?
assertions: An HTML file is written that works on its own offline: it loads no script, stylesheet or font from a CDN or any http(s) URL

The diagram shows the order path the code shows: the web checkout posting to the API's POST /orders, the API validating and inserting into Postgres, pushing an email job onto the Redis 'emails' list, and the worker popping it and posting to the mailer service
Kafka does not appear as part of the order path; if it is mentioned at all, it is described as planned in the README and not in the code
No payment step or payment provider appears in the order path (the README says payment is taken in the shop on collection)
It does not add parts the repo does not contain, such as a load balancer, CDN, auth service, cache or separate analytics service
The parts or connections in the diagram, or the page's text, name the files they come from (for example api/app.py, worker/worker.py, web/checkout.js, docker-compose.yml)
Anything drawn that the code does not show (for example who hosts the mailer, or what happens after the email is sent) is marked as an assumption, or left off
The reply opens with where the file is and what the diagram shows, in a few sentences, without a long account of how it was built

Finance then checks the receipts match and pays it in the next payroll run. Claims older than 90 days are rejected automatically when you submit them.
assertions: An HTML file is written that works on its own offline, loading nothing from a CDN or any http(s) URL

The flow includes, in order: submit in the finance portal with receipts, the automatic rejection of claims older than 90 days, line manager approval, the over £500 decision leading to finance director approval, finance checking receipts, and payment in the next payroll run
The over £500 rule and the 90-day rule are drawn as decisions or branches, not as plain steps

What happens when the line manager or finance director declines, or when receipts don't match, is not stated in the description, so it is either left off or visibly marked as an assumption, never drawn as a definite step
It adds no steps, roles, systems or thresholds the description does not contain (for example no budget-holder step, no expense card, no second threshold)
The reply is short: where the file is, what it shows, and which paths were not covered by the description

evals.prompt:
Can you make an interactive sequence diagram of how a repair request goes through at Fernhill Housing Co-op? I want to show it to our board next week as one file they can open. Here's how it works as far as I know:

A tenant phones the contact centre or fills in the web form to report a repair. The contact centre logs it in our housing management system (HMS) and gives the tenant a reference number. Every weekday morning the repairs coordinator goes through the new jobs in HMS, decides the priority (emergency = attend within 24 hours, routine = within 20 working days) and assigns it to one of our two contractors by emailing them the job sheet. The contractor rings the tenant to book a visit, then does the work. After the visit the contractor marks the job complete in their own portal. At the end of each month the contractor sends us an invoice listing the jobs they finished, and finance closes those jobs in HMS when they pay the invoice.

If the contractor needs to order parts I'm honestly not sure what happens, I think they tell the coordinator? We used to post the tenant a confirmation letter when a job was closed but we stopped doing that in 2025. There's also the annual gas safety check programme but that's a different process, leave it out.
assertions: Writes one self-contained HTML file that opens offline: no <script src>, <link href>, @import or font URL pointing at http(s), and the diagram's code and styles are inline

It is a sequence diagram with at least these participants: tenant, contact centre, HMS, repairs coordinator, contractor and finance (the contractor's portal may be its own participant or part of the contractor)

The messages run in this order: tenant reports by phone or web form; contact centre logs the job in HMS and gives the tenant a reference number; the coordinator reviews new jobs each weekday morning, sets the priority (emergency 24 hours, routine 20 working days) and emails the job sheet to a contractor; the contractor rings the tenant to book and does the visit; the contractor marks the job complete in its own portal; the contractor sends a monthly invoice to finance; finance closes the jobs in HMS on payment
The parts-ordering step is drawn dashed or labelled as an assumption or unconfirmed (the user said they are not sure), not as a solid confirmed message
The posted confirmation letter does not appear as a current step (absent, or shown only as stopped in 2025), and the gas safety check programme does not appear

Points out at least one hand-off gap the description reveals: nothing tells the tenant the repair is finished or closed; HMS only learns a job is done when finance pays the monthly invoice, so jobs stay open in HMS for weeks; or an emergency reported after the morning review waits until the next weekday morning before the coordinator sees it

Each message carries or cites the words from the user's description it came from, and the diagram adds no participants or systems the user did not describe (for example no SMS service, CRM, scheduling tool or tenant app)
The reply opens with where the HTML file is and the main takeaway (such as the gap found), not with a long account of how the diagram was made

evals.prompt:
I coordinate adoptions at a small animal rescue (call it Hollyford Rescue) and I'd love an interactive diagram of our adoption process to share with new volunteers. Here's how it goes, as best I can explain it:

Someone spots an animal on our website and fills in the online enquiry. A volunteer rings them within 3 days for a chat. If it sounds like a fit we email them the full application form; if not, we point them to other rescues. When the application comes back we take up two references - one has to be their vet if they've had pets before. Then there's a home visit. We do a home visit for every adoption, except cats going to someone who's adopted from us before - unless they've moved house since, in which case we do it again. After that comes a meet-and-greet at the shelter, and dogs also meet any dog already living in the household. The adoption panel sits on Thursdays and approves or declines. If they decline we email the applicant, and they can reapply after 3 months. If approved, we hold the animal for them for 48 hours. They pay the fee (150 pounds for dogs, 90 for cats) and sign the adoption contract. Our vet does a final health check and transfers the microchip, then it's collection day. We ring them two weeks after collection, and someone visits at six months.
assertions: Writes one self-contained .html file that opens offline: no <script src>, stylesheet link, @import or font URL pointing at http(s) or a CDN

All the steps appear in the order described, none merged away: online enquiry, phone chat within 3 days, application form emailed, application returned, two references, home visit, meet-and-greet, Thursday panel, 48-hour hold, fee and contract, vet check and microchip transfer, collection, two-week call, six-month visit

Gets the home-visit rule right: a home visit by default; skipped only for a cat going to a previous adopter who has not moved house; dogs always get one; a previous cat adopter who has moved gets one again. It does not draw 'previous adopters skip the home visit' without the cat and moved-house conditions
Shows the two branches the user gave: not a fit after the phone chat -> pointed to other rescues; panel declines -> email, can reapply after 3 months. The panel step says it sits on Thursdays

Gets the smaller conditions right: the vet must be one of the two references only if the applicant has had pets before; only dogs meet the household's resident dog; the fee is 150 pounds for a dog and 90 for a cat

Flags the gap: the description never says what happens if the 48 hours run out before the fee is paid and the contract signed. That outcome is drawn dashed or marked as an open question, and the reply raises it, rather than being drawn as a solid step

Nothing is invented: no step, fee, deposit, timing, role or outcome the user didn't describe (for example no path for a failed reference or a failed home visit) is drawn as fact; anything like that is dashed and labelled as an assumption. Steps cite the user's own words as their source

The reply's first line is the path or link to the HTML file, followed straight away by the takeaway (such as the 48-hour gap or the home-visit exception); no build log, tool output or status report comes before it
